1. This Act may be cited as the Registration of Guests Act,
1965, and shall come into forde on the Ist day of October,
1965, and shall extend throughout Malaysia.

2. In this Act, unless the context otherwise requires—

"identity card" means an identity card issued under the
National Registration Act, 1959, or other similar document
identifying the holder thereof

"keeper", in respect of any specified premises, includes the
proprietor and manager thereof and any person for the
time being authorised to permit persons to lodge in those
premises;

"lodge" includes, in relation to a room in any specified
premises ordinarily used as| sleeping accommodation by
persons lodging thereat, the occupation of any such room
by a person required to be registered under section 3 (1) (a)
(whether by day or by night)/for any period of time;

"passport" includes any similar travel document;

"registration officer" means|a registration officer appointed
under the National Registration Act, 1959, or under any
corresponding law in force in Sabah or Sarawak;

_"specified premises" mears any premises, whether fur-
nished or unfurnished, where lodging or sleeping accommo-
dation is provided for reward.

3. (1) It shall be the duty of] the keeper of any specified
premises—                   |
(a) to keep a register in the form in the First Schedule
of all persons lodging at the premises who are
not servants of the] keeper of the premises and
who are not under the age of twelve years;

(5) on the arrival of any/such person at the premises,
to ascertain and enter or cause to be entered in
the register kept for that purpose the name,
address, occupation, sex and nationality of that
person, and the number, place and date of issue
of his identity card jor (if he has no identity card)
of his passport, together with the date and time
of his arrival and the name of the last place from
which, and the means by which, he arrived;

(c) on the departure off any such person from the
premises, to enter pr cause to be entered in the
register the date and time of departure and the
destination on depprture of such person;

(d) to enter or cause to be entered in the register such
other particulars a$ may be prescribed; and

(e) to furnish to the nearest registration officer such
returns as to the persons lodging at the premises
at such times or intervals and in such form as
may be prescribed

(2) It shall be the duty of every person required to be
registered under subsection (Il) (a) to furnish the particulars
required by this Act to be entered in the register and to
sign the register.

(3) Every register kept/urider this section shall be open
at all reasonable hours for inspection by any police officer,
registration officer or any person authorised in that behalf
by 2, registration Officer. 1

"(4) Every register kept under this section shall be pre-
served by the keeper of the premises to which it relates
for a period of not less than two years from the date of
the last entry and may thereafter, at the discretion of the
keeper, be destroyed.

(5) Notwithstanding anything contained in this section,
the registration officer may,| by notice in writing under his
hand, authorize the keeper of any specified premises
mentioned in the notice to} keep a register in a different
form (including a loose-leaf register or card-index or a
register which is partly in the form of a bound register and
partly in the form of a lopse-leaf register or card-index)
from that provided by this section.

4, (1) Any keeper of any specified premises who—

(a) fails to enter or cause to be entered in the register
any particulars which he is required by this Act
to enter or cause to be entered therein; ‘or

(6) fails to furnish to a revistration officer any return
which he is required by this Act to furnish; or

(c) obstructs any police officer or any person autho-
rised by a registratidn officer when such officer
or person is exercising his functions under this
Act,

shall be guilty of an offence and on conviction shall be
liable to imprisonment for|a term not exceeding one year
or to a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars, or to both.

—_

(2) Any person who—

(a) knowingly or recklessly makes, or causes or per-
mits to be made, in dny register or in any return
any statement which is false in a material
particular; or

(b) without the approval/jof the registration officer,
wilfully destroys, or |mutilates or obliterates any-
thing in, any register shall be guilty of an offence
and on conviction shall be liable to imprisonment
for a term not exc¢dding one year or to a fine
not exceeding two thousand dollars, or to both.

(3) Any person required to be registered under section
3 (1) (a) who contravenes the |provisions of section 3 (2)
shall be guilty of an offence and on conviction shall be
liable to imprisonment for a tarm not exceeding one year
or to a fine not exceeding two thousand dollars, or to both.

5. The Minister may make rule$ for carrying into effect the
provisions of this Act and, in particular and without pre-
judice to the generality of the floregoing, such rules may—

(a) provide for anything |which may be prescribed
